assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: Response has two tables ('Reis Discount Tier', 'Discount by Passenger Type') but no rolling window table; rolling window boundary is listed as an open question

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented — either as a row in the eligibility table or a separate note.
assertions.evidence: 'Child — flat discount, no travel history | Child | 0 | 20%' and 'Child — flat discount regardless of travel | Child | {4, 20, 40} | 20%' rows

assertions.text: The discount ladder has multiple tiers derived from the 'every fifth trip' rule, with boundary values or value sets showing which ticket counts produce which discount. The maximum 40% discount is represented.
assertions.evidence: Multiple tiers shown (0%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 40%), boundary values at 0, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 20, 40, 45, and 'At maximum tier | 40 | 40%'

assertions.text: The 30-day rolling window boundary is tested: a ticket at exactly 30 days is included, at 31 days is excluded.
assertions.evidence: No rolling window table exists; response lists this as an open question: 'Rolling window edge: If exactly 30 days ago...'

assertions.text: Value sets in the tier table contain exactly the values that produce the same discount. No cross-tier contamination.
assertions.evidence: 'Reis Discount Tier' table has no value sets; uses individual rows '5 | 5%', '7 | 5%', '9 | 5%' instead of grouped values

assertions.text: The discount ladder table uses value sets for the ticket count column to group counts within the same tier (e.g. {5, 6, 7, 8, 9} or {5, 9} for min/max → 5%) — not one row per boundary value.
assertions.evidence: 'At first discount threshold | 5 | 5%', 'Mid first tier | 7 | 5%', 'Top of first tier | 9 | 5%' are separate rows; no value sets used

assertions.text: The tier-to-discount mapping is expressed once — not repeated across multiple tables.
assertions.evidence: Both 'Reis Discount Tier' and 'Discount by Passenger Type' tables express that ticket counts 5+ map to 5% discount, duplicating the tier mapping

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: Response contains markdown tables, not Java code; no @DisplayName annotations present

assertions.text: @Description is present on at least the class or the tier method and provides context beyond what the table rows already express.
Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Response has no Java annotations; tables are in markdown format

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description is absent from response, assertion passes vacuously

assertions.text: The eligibility/passenger-type table includes a Zone column (or equivalent) with a value set to show that the discount applies regardless of zone.
assertions.evidence: 'Zones Do Not Affect Discount' table has Zone column but separate rows '1 zone' and '3 zones' instead of value set

assertions.text: Adult and senior are expressed as a value set {ADULT, SENIOR} (or equivalent) in at least one row of the eligibility table.
assertions.evidence: 'Adult — at first tier | Adult | 4 | 5%' and 'Senior — same ladder as adult | Senior | 4 | 5%' are enumerated as separate rows

assertions.text: Each tier in the discount ladder is expressed as a single row with a value set for ticket counts — not split across multiple rows.
assertions.evidence: 5% tier split across 'At first discount threshold | 5 | 5%', 'Mid first tier | 7 | 5%', 'Top of first tier | 9 | 5%' rows

assertions.text: The rolling window table expresses time relatively (e.g. '14 days ago', '30 days ago', or an integer 'Days ago' column).
assertions.evidence: No rolling window table exists; response mentions 'last 30 days' in text but no dedicated boundary-testing table

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table mixing unrelated rules.
assertions.evidence: Three separate tables: 'Reis Discount Tier', 'Discount by Passenger Type', 'Zones Do Not Affect Discount'

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations from combining concerns.
